subject: Mathematics
central_question: How can antiderivatives and definite integrals be found systematically using standard formulas, integration techniques and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus?
in_scope_units: 7.1 Introduction: indefinite and definite integrals as the two parts of integral calculus.
7.2 Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation and properties of indefinite integrals.
7.3 Methods of Integration: inspection and substitution.
7.7 Integrals involving standard quadratic radical forms.
7.8 Definite Integral and area interpretation as a limit of sums.
7.10 Evaluation of Definite Integrals by Substitution.
banned_topics: Area between curves as a separate application chapter

known_pitfalls.claim: An indefinite integral has one unique answer.
known_pitfalls.correction: It represents a family F(x)+C of antiderivatives.

known_pitfalls.claim: The constant of integration can be omitted.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is essential in indefinite integrals because functions with the same derivative differ by a constant.

known_pitfalls.claim: Integration by parts is product rule without order considerations.
known_pitfalls.correction: The choice of first and second factors strongly affects the work.

known_pitfalls.claim: A definite integral always equals geometric area.
known_pitfalls.correction: It gives signed accumulation; portions below the x-axis contribute negatively.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Example 1 in Section 7.2 to integrate by inspection.
Use a substitution example from Section 7.3.
Use the Fundamental Theorem and a property of definite integrals for final evaluation.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter contains Exercises 7.1 to 7.11 followed by the Miscellaneous Exercise on Chapter 7.
